settings.account: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.
settings.members: Who can sign in to this VPN, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also add people and devices and end sessions; admins also remove people and manage groups, IP groups, members and tokens.
settings.signin: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.
settings.tokens: For scripts and the command line tool. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
settings.askAdmin: Ask an admin of this VPN for access.

people.title: People
people.description: Everyone who may connect. Each device of a person gets its own certificate and fixed VPN address; their groups decide which networks it reaches.
people.noGroups: No groups yet. Admins add them under Access.
people.emptyBody: Add a person, then a device for them, and send them the .ovpn file it gives you.
people.addBody: They get devices that may connect. Signing in to this VPN product is under Members.
people.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}}? Their devices are revoked and disconnected, and this cannot be undone.
people.confirmSuspend: Suspend {{name}}? Their devices are disconnected within 15 seconds and cannot connect until you activate them again.
people.suspendedBody: None of their devices can connect. Activate them to let their devices back in; their certificates stay valid.
people.groupsBody: Which IP groups their devices reach comes from these.

devices.confirmRevoke: Revoke {{name}}? It is disconnected within 15 seconds and its .ovpn file stops working for good.
devices.description: One certificate per device, valid for a year. A lost or replaced device is revoked; add a new one for the new device.
devices.addedTitle: Device added. Send its file now
devices.addedBody: {{file}} downloaded. It holds the device's private key; they import it into an OpenVPN client.
devices.notKept: This VPN does not keep the file
devices.notKeptBody: It cannot be downloaded again once this dialog closes. Send it privately.
devices.addBody: It gets its own certificate and VPN address. Its .ovpn file downloads once.
devices.noneYetBody: Add one; you get its .ovpn file once.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Devices connected now, as each server reports them every 15 seconds. Ending a session disconnects it at the next heartbeat; the device may connect again while it is allowed. To keep it out, revoke the device or suspend the person.

access.title: Access
access.description: People are in groups; an IP group lists networks and ports and the groups that may reach them. A device gets routes to those networks only, and the server's firewall drops everything else from it.
access.confirmRemoveGroup: Remove the group {{name}}? Its {{count}} people lose the access it gave them.
access.groupsBody: Add people to groups on their page.
access.addGroupBody: Add people to it on their page, and let it reach networks under IP groups.
access.confirmRemoveIpGroup: Remove the IP group {{name}}? Devices lose the routes and firewall rules it gave them.
access.ipGroupsBody: Servers apply a change within one heartbeat, without disconnecting anyone.
access.noIpGroups: No IP groups yet: devices connect but reach nothing
access.editorBody: Networks and ports, and the groups that may reach them.
access.fullTunnelBody: Send all of the device's traffic through the VPN, not only these networks. Use it where traffic must leave from the office address.
access.allowedGroups: Groups that may reach these networks

servers.worksOnce: It works once, until {{date}}, and is not shown again.
servers.onHost: On the host clients connect to:
servers.onHostAt: On the host clients connect to ({{address}}):
servers.keepVolume: Keep the volume: the server's secret is in it. For TCP 443, add
servers.insteadOfUdp: instead of the UDP port. Next to this VPN with its compose file, set the token in the server's variable, for example
servers.clientConfigs: Client configs list a server once it has reported. Devices added before that do not know it; they keep using the servers they have.
servers.closingHides: Closing this dialog hides the token
servers.closingHidesBody: If it is lost, enrol the server again from its row.
servers.promptAddress: Address clients connect to for {{id}}. Leave empty to use VPN_PUBLIC_HOST. Client configs made before keep the old address.
servers.confirmEnrolLegacy: Enrol {{id}} with its own secret? VPN_SERVER_TOKEN stops working for it now: start it again with the token you get next.
servers.confirmEnrolAgain: Enrol {{id}} again? Its secret stops working now, and it gets a new certificate once you start it with the new token.
servers.confirmRemove: Remove {{id}}? It stops getting its config and its sessions end. Client configs that list it skip to the next server.
servers.legacyTitle: Uses the shared VPN_SERVER_TOKEN. Enrol it to give it its own secret.
servers.title: Servers
servers.description: vpn-server runs OpenVPN on the hosts clients connect to, here or at other locations. Each pulls its config from here and reports every 15 seconds; client configs list every server, so clients move to the next one when one is down. It must have the same version as this VPN.
servers.addBody: Its address is the host name or IP clients connect to; leave it empty to use VPN_PUBLIC_HOST.
servers.noneYetBody: Add one, then start vpn-server with its token; it shows up within 15 seconds.
